title: OLMo 2: A Fully Open Model
hook: Ai2's OLMo 2 is fully open — not just weights, but the training data, code, and checkpoints — the strongest reproducible-from-scratch model for researchers.
key_points: From the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2): 7B and 13B in late 2024, a 32B in March 2025.
'Fully open' — weights, training data, code, recipes, and intermediate checkpoints all released.
The 32B was the first fully open model to rival GPT-3.5-Turbo / GPT-4o-mini on academic benchmarks.
Lets researchers audit, replicate, and build on the entire training pipeline.
content_html: OLMo 2, from the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2), pushes a stricter notion of "open" than most so-called open models. Where releases like Llama publish weights but keep the training data and recipe private, OLMo 2 releases everything — weights, the full training data, the training and fine-tuning code, and intermediate checkpoints — so the entire model can be reproduced and audited from scratch.
extra_html:
What's new

The family launched with 7B and 13B models in late 2024 and added a 32B model in March 2025. Trained on trillions of tokens with a focus on training stability and data quality, the 32B was notable for being the first fully open model to match or beat strong commercial baselines like GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4o-mini on a suite of academic benchmarks — closing much of the gap while keeping the whole pipeline transparent.

Why it matters

"Open weights" and "open source" are not the same thing. OLMo 2 is genuinely the latter: the data and code that produced it are public, which makes it a uniquely valuable artifact for science — you can study exactly how capabilities emerge, not just the finished model. That transparency is the point, and it is rare at this scale.

related.title: The Pile: 800GB of Diverse Text
related.hook: Web text alone leaves gaps. The Pile stitches together 22 curated sources — academic and professional — so a language model picks up knowledge plain web crawls miss.

related.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
related.hook: Meta's Llama 3 family, trained on roughly 15 trillion tokens with a 405B-parameter flagship, narrowed the gap to closed frontier models while staying open-weights.

related.title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes LMs Better
related.hook: Training corpora are full of copies — one 61-word sentence shows up 60,000+ times in C4. Strip the duplicates and models memorize far less and evaluate more honestly.

flashcards.prompt: How does OLMo 2's 'fully open' differ from open-weights releases like Llama?

choices.text: It releases weights plus training data, code, recipes, and checkpoints — the whole pipeline
It releases only the weights, like Llama
It keeps the weights private but publishes the data

flashcards.explanation_html: Llama publishes weights but keeps data and recipe private; OLMo 2 releases everything so the model can be reproduced and audited.

flashcards.prompt: Why is OLMo 2 described as uniquely valuable for science?
flashcards.back_html: Because its data and code are public, you can study exactly how capabilities emerge, not just the finished model — rare at this scale.
